name: Heavy Dumbbell Suitcase Row
description: The heavy dumbbell suitcase row is performed with the dumbbell at the side of the body (like carrying a suitcase) while bent over, rowing the weight upward in a path parallel to the torso rather than toward the hip. The unique line of pull challenges the mid and lower trapezius and rhomboids through a range often undertrained in standard dumbbell rows.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet shoulder width apart. Hold a heavy dumbbell in one hand at the side, as if holding a suitcase. Hinge at the hips to 45-60 degrees, allowing the dumbbell to hang beside the working hip.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a heavy dumbbell — typically heavier than standard rows since the range of motion is shorter. The free hand can rest on the thigh for light support.
steps: Step 1: Begin hinged with the dumbbell hanging beside the hip.
Step 2: Row the dumbbell directly upward, keeping it close to the thigh and torso.
Step 3: Drive the elbow upward rather than backward — the motion is more vertical than horizontal.
Step 4: At the top, the elbow should be at torso height with the forearm vertical.
Step 5: Lower under control and repeat.
common_mistakes: Pulling the dumbbell toward the chest rather than straight up alongside the body
Allowing the torso to rotate excessively — control anti-rotation
safety_considerations: Maintain neutral spine throughout — heavy loads demand braced core
Avoid if experiencing lower back pain until cleared
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Dumbbell at full arm extension beside hip to elbow at torso height.
coaching_cues: Row straight up — not back, not forward
Keep the dumbbell close to the thigh throughout
Drive the elbow toward the ceiling
